page: Amazon Web Services c6id.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz across 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores with 2 threads per core). The processor supports hardware acceleration extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI, supplemented by 54 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. System memory comprises 32 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, providing an explicit ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

Unlike diskless compute instances, the c6id.4xlarge bundles 950 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. The hardware contains no dedicated GPU accelerators. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the instance demonstrates mid-tier, balanced execution, scoring 1643.0 in Geekbench single-core and 9833.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 21278.81. Data handling capabilities are underscored by 15.68 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 21.31 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency is tied directly to the balance of compute performance and low-latency attached NVMe storage. By delivering high compute density alongside bundled high-speed physical storage, it reduces the operational overhead and external volume costs typical of storage-intensive compute pipelines. However, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio imposes a memory ceiling, making it unsuitable for massive in-memory databases, and the absence of GPU acceleration limits large-scale AI training. Optimal workloads include software compilation, media transcoding, static web serving, high-throughput key-value stores, and batch data processing requiring fast temporary storage.
